ideas.title: Lambda fits low-traffic agent tools
ideas.post_angle: AWS Lambda is a good fit for small internal agent tools that are used occasionally because you pay per invocation instead of running an always-on server.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the clearest continuation from the previous Railway workshop and gives practitioners a deployment trade-off they can reuse.

source_moments.note: Railway-style deployment means an always-on server; Lambda only charges for invocation.
The deployed Lambda app works and the cost model is explained for rarely used tools.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a practical post about using Lambda for low-traffic agent tools and the cost trade-off versus always-on hosting.

ideas.title: Isolate AWS before giving agents credentials
ideas.post_angle: Before letting a coding agent touch AWS, isolate the experiment from production with a separate account and short-lived, project-scoped credentials.
ideas.why_worth_posting: The transcript has a concrete security workflow and a useful discussion about why global environment credentials are risky.

source_moments.note: The remote machine has no production AWS access; a separate AWS account is created for experiments.
Trust is bounded by keeping the agent away from production.
Temporary STS credentials are preferred for a session.
Project-local credentials are compared with global shell environment variables.

ideas.title: AI engineers still own the code
ideas.post_angle: Using coding agents is becoming normal, but the engineer still owns the system and must understand, document, and review what the agent did.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is a high-level but practical career and workflow lesson from the session.

source_moments.note: AI engineers are expected to use coding tools but still understand the output.
Agent-generated work should be documented so it can be repeated without the agent.
Documentation matters when the path involved experimentation.
Generated documentation should still be cleaned and processed.

clip.title: You still own the code
clip.reason: This is the clearest statement of the workflow expectation for AI engineers.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about agent-assisted engineering where the engineer uses agents but keeps ownership of the system.

ideas.title: FastAPI to custom Lambda runtime for SSE
ideas.post_angle: Moving the previous FastAPI app to Lambda required replacing the web layer with custom routing and a custom runtime because SSE streaming is not the default Lambda path.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the main technical architecture lesson of the workshop.

source_moments.note: The goal is to serve frontend, backend, and streaming events through Lambda.
The Lambda handler routes GET/POST paths and streams ask responses.
A custom runtime is needed because the default path is buffered.

clip.reason: This segment explains handler routing and why Lambda is lower-level than FastAPI.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a technical post explaining what changed when moving a streaming agent app from FastAPI to Lambda.

ideas.title: Let the agent get it working, then simplify
ideas.post_angle: A useful agent workflow is to let the agent produce a working version, commit it, then read and simplify the parts you do not understand.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This captures the realistic workflow from the session: fast progress first, followed by review and simplification.

source_moments.note: The first working version is committed, then simplified and understood.
Agents can create complex abstractions, so references and review help control output.
Before using this in real apps, every Lambda-specific line should be understood.

clip.title: Working first, simplification second

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post about using agents to get a working version quickly, then simplifying and reviewing it before treating it as production code.

ideas.title: Lambda deployment has small hidden gotchas
ideas.post_angle: Deploying a Lambda container is not only code changes. You need ECR, CloudFormation, the Lambda runtime, local testing, and even Docker image metadata details.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is a practical checklist-style post for engineers who expect Lambda deployment to be a single command.

source_moments.note: The deployment creates ECR, pushes the image, and succeeds after agent-assisted fixes.
The deploy scripts, CloudFormation, ECR, Lambda URL, and Docker provenance issue are discussed.
The custom bootstrap and exec process are explained.
